facts: Gradient and angle of inclination are linked by $m = \tan\theta$, where $0^{\circ} \le \theta < 180^{\circ}$ and $\theta \ne 90^{\circ}$.
A positive gradient gives an acute angle, and $\theta = \tan^{-1}(m)$.
A vertical line has $\theta = 90^{\circ}$ and no gradient.

Exact values: $m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ gives $30^{\circ}$, $m = 1$ gives $45^{\circ}$, $m = \sqrt{3}$ gives $60^{\circ}$, $m = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ gives $150^{\circ}$, $m = -1$ gives $135^{\circ}$, and $m = -\sqrt{3}$ gives $120^{\circ}$.
steps: Differentiate $f(x)$ to find the gradient $m = f'(x_1)$
If $m < 0$, add $180^{\circ}$ to the calculator result to obtain the obtuse angle in $[0^{\circ}, 180^{\circ})$

workedExamples.question_text: Find the gradients of the tangents to $y = x^2 - 4x + 2$ at $x = 1$ and $x = 3$, then find their angles of inclination to the nearest minute.
Find, to the nearest minute, the angles of inclination of the tangents to $y = 9 - x^2$ at its $x$-intercepts.
workedExamples.solution_text:
At the $x$-intercepts, $y = 0$.
$\begin{aligned}9 - x^2 &= 0 \\ x^2 &= 9 \\ x &= -3 \text{ or } x = 3\end{aligned}$

$f'(x) = -2x$

At $(-3,0)$:
$m = f'(-3) = 6$
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta &= 6 \\ \theta &= \tan^{-1}(6) \\ &\approx 80.5377^{\circ} \\ &\approx 80^{\circ}32'\end{aligned}$

At $(3,0)$:
$m = f'(3) = -6$
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta &= -6 \\ \theta &= 180^{\circ} + \tan^{-1}(-6) \\ &\approx 99.4623^{\circ} \\ &\approx 99^{\circ}28'\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Find any points on $y = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - 8$ where the tangent has an angle of inclination of $45^{\circ}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$m = \tan 45^{\circ} = 1$

$f'(x) = x^2$
$\begin{aligned}x^2 &= 1 \\ x &= 1 \text{ or } x = -1\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}f(1) &= \dfrac{1}{3} - 8 \\ &= -\dfrac{23}{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}f(-1) &= -\dfrac{1}{3} - 8 \\ &= -\dfrac{25}{3}\end{aligned}$

The points are $\left(1,-\dfrac{23}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-1,-\dfrac{25}{3}\right)$.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the point on $y = 4\sqrt{x}$ where the tangent has an angle of inclination of $60^{\circ}$.

Find the exact angle of inclination of the tangent to each curve at the given value of $x$.

(a) $y = x^2 - 7x + 2$ at $x = 3$.

(b) $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x\sqrt{x}$ at $x = 12$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)
$f'(x) = 2x - 7$
$\begin{aligned}m &= f'(3) \\ &= 2(3) - 7 \\ &= -1\end{aligned}$

$\tan\theta = -1$

The angle of inclination is obtuse, so $\theta = 135^{\circ}$.

(b)
$y = \dfrac{1}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}}$
$\begin{aligned}f'(x) &= \dfrac{1}{2}x^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ &= \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}m &= f'(12) \\ &= \dfrac{\sqrt{12}}{2} \\ &= \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

$\tan\theta = \sqrt{3}$

The angle of inclination is acute, so $\theta = 60^{\circ}$.

development.question_text: Find the angle of inclination of the tangent to $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 - 2x$ at $x = 1$.
Find the angle of inclination of the tangent to $y = x^3 - x$ at $x = 2$, correct to the nearest minute.
Find the angle of inclination of the tangent to $y = 4 - x^2$ at its positive $x$-intercept $(2, 0)$, correct to the nearest minute.
Find the coordinates of the two points on the curve $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 - 3x + 1$ where the tangent has an angle of inclination of $45^{\circ}$.
development.solution_text:
$m = \tan 45^{\circ} = 1$
$f'(x) = x^2 - 3$
$x^2 - 3 = 1$
$x^2 = 4$
$x = 2 \text{ or } x = -2$
For $x = 2$: $y = \dfrac{1}{3}(2)^3 - 3(2) + 1 = \dfrac{8}{3} - 6 + 1 = -\dfrac{7}{3}$
The point is $\left(2, -\dfrac{7}{3}\right)$.
For $x = -2$: $y = \dfrac{1}{3}(-2)^3 - 3(-2) + 1 = -\dfrac{8}{3} + 6 + 1 = \dfrac{13}{3}$
The point is $\left(-2, \dfrac{13}{3}\right)$.
The points are $\left(2, -\dfrac{7}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-2, \dfrac{13}{3}\right)$.
